Only adjacent scaffolding exists: plannerDocuments (workspaceId-keyed BlockSuite metadata with no gateway or frontend consumer), thread-scoped Model Plane todos (todo.rs; read-only in the chat run panel with a status-update proxy), org-scoped capability-core /api/v1/tasks, and support tickets with saved ticket-views. The item's agent-write path is not a simple tool: Control currently supports exactly one agent owner action (tickets.create), so a records write is a new owner-action vertical.

constraints: Convex does not evaluate Space roles (spaces.ts says Space roles are not a Convex-tracked concept; the gateway verifies live Control membership and Convex only re-verifies org membership with the service key), so 'Control decisions gate every query and mutation' must be implemented as gateway-side Control decisions for new record read/write effects, not inside convex-core. Records are content, so the new table must join the Space deletion owner-receipt flow and the ZDR rule, unlike presence and read markers which are content-free. ADR rows 84-85 forbid a second generic project authority and treat planner workspaceId as a resource-local partition, so records must hang off spaceRef and not reuse plannerDocuments, workspaceId or the Convex projects table. Assignees must be Control subject ids (space_memberships allows user and service subjects); ticket or document links must be refs whose access is rechecked by the owner plane on read, since Space access never widens an owner ACL. Model proposes, owner executes: an agent may only propose record changes, and Control resolves a single supported owner action today (model_action_view.go), with the browser Model allowlist still empty.
approachAdjustment: Ship human-edited records first (table view, typed columns, assignees, saved views, per-record thread later) with gateway-side Control decisions, and take the agent create/update path out of this item: it needs a new owner-action vertical (schema hash, run-bound decision with payload digest, owner verifier, approval continuation) like tickets.create. Reuse the Todo status vocabulary instead of inventing a new one, register the table in the Space deletion flow, and keep authority-bearing fields human-only.
effortNote: L holds only for the human-edited table, assignees and saved views; the agent write path is a separate L-to-XL vertical blocked on the S2 owner-action framework, so bundling it makes this XL.
verdictReason: Status is absent (confirmed in schema, route table and cockpit tabs), but the approach misstates how agents write records and where Space authority is enforced, and bundles an owner-action vertical into a table feature.

exactGap: Control user-core already stores a per-user NotificationSettings.QuietHours {enabled, start, end} (default off, 22:00-08:00) and a manual profile availability status (online/busy/away/offline, labelled as helpdesk behaviour), but nothing enforces or exposes them: the frontend has no quiet-hours UI and notification-core's only gate is a per-event opt-out (WithPreferenceGate, IsNotificationEnabled) with no time window, DND, VIP or urgency class. No Space event producers reach notification-core either (the sender allow-list is gateway 'notification.created' for the delegated user and capability-core run_completed/run_failed), and a gate-suppressed request is stored as suppressed and returns before dispatch, so it neither reaches push nor creates an inbox row.
reuse: user-core NotificationSettings and QuietHours (GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/notifications) as the source of truth to extend with timezone, days, dnd_until and VIP
notification-core WithPreferenceGate seam in Accept (service.go isNotificationEnabled) as the enforcement point, and the existing suppressed status
notification-core identity_sync NATS consumer as the pattern for projecting a user attention setting from Control into notification-core
AccountSettingsPage Availability section as the UI host and the existing profile status field
activity-grammar.ts salience classes (critical, attention, normal, muted) as the urgency vocabulary for approval and awaiting signals
constraints: DND is a person-level attribute that spans organisations, while notification-core rows and every Space or Model event are org-scoped, so keep the source of truth in Control user-core and project it into notification-core by event or API, never by cross-plane DB read. The existing gate is binary (suppressed or sent) and drops the inbox row too, so DND needs a tri-state (deliver, inbox-only, deferred) and a flush path; the delivery queue is off by default and rejects ZDR requests, so flush depends on finishing the S4.4 ledger (F-t1-060). Urgency must be set by the trusted producer (gateway or capability-core), not by the agent, with a per-agent cap; the 'interruptible now' answer to agents must be a narrow server-side read bound to the run's delegated subject that does not disclose the schedule or cross orgs. Quiet hours are already named in S4.4, and space-defenition.md lists 'notification polish' in its non-goals, so this is planned but only partly aligned with the stated non-goal.
approachAdjustment: Start from the existing user-core quiet-hours setting instead of a new attention-state table: add timezone (the profile already has one), days, dnd_until and VIP, project it into notification-core, and add the gate after the preference check with a deliver/inbox-only/defer decision. Sequence it after the Space notification producers (F-t1-008) exist, because there is nothing Space-specific to gate today, and fold the deferred flush into the single S4.4 ledger rather than a second queue.
effortNote: M holds for settings, gate and UI; the flush rides on the S4.4 ledger (F-t1-060) and the producers are separate items.
verdictReason: The item says no quiet hours exist, but a stored-and-unenforced per-user quiet-hours setting and a profile availability status already exist in Control; the build should extend them and respect the person-level versus org-scoped split.

exactGap: notification-core has a leased delivery-attempt state machine (pending, claimed, sent_unconfirmed, acknowledged, failed, unknown), a lease-fenced worker and request-level idempotency keys, but the worker is off by default, needs NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_MODE=novu plus a callback secret, has no bounded-retry or max-age policy, and rejects ZDR requests outright (service.go:296-301, delivery_worker.go:91-94). The Space delivery ledger is a named gap (delivery_ledger_not_built, spaces.rs:1618-1623) with no Space-event producers, and no per-user digest exists: insight-core's daily-brief scheduler (per-org/day idempotency key, email channel registered in migration 006) is deliberately disabled because an organisation is not a notification recipient.
reuse: notification-core delivery_attempts state machine, lease-fenced worker and callback verifier as the single ledger (do not build a parallel Space ledger)
notification-core request idempotency keys (FindByIdempotencyKey and resumeExisting) and insight-core BriefIdempotencyKey (daily_brief_<org>_<day>) as the digest dedupe pattern
insight-core briefs scheduler shape (round per tick, per-recipient key) and the channel-config registry rows for email (migrations 006 and 013)
Convex outbox lease pattern (spaceLifecycleEvents deliveryState, lease, nextAttemptAt) and ctx.scheduler.runAfter workers for a Space-side outbox or digest tick
notification-core identity_sync consumer pattern for event-fed user state
constraints: ZDR: notification-core refuses to enqueue ZDR requests today because the queue stores no payload and no transient-descriptor provider contract exists, so a ZDR org's counts-and-links digest cannot ride the existing queue; it needs an explicit content-free request class or retention mode ruled on by Control/ZDR policy, or the encrypted expiry-bound descriptor contract the code comment names. Email goes through Novu to an external provider, a content-persisting boundary whose provider and ZDR proof the S4.4 tracker still lists as open. Recipients must be real user subjects (the gateway may notify only the delegated user; an org id is not a recipient), and digest counts must come from Application-owned state (read markers, inbox feed) or owner-plane APIs and events, never DB reads, since pending approvals live in Model Plane. Digest links must resolve through normal Space membership checks (membership_changed revocations apply), so Space access never widens.
approachAdjustment: Treat finishing the S4.4 ledger (bounded retries, max-age, ZDR proof, durable feed reconciliation, HA) as the already-planned dependency rather than new work, and make the digest a separate Application Plane item: a per-user scheduler modelled on insight-core's briefs scheduler (using Convex scheduler or an outbox) that composes counts and links, instead of a capability-core Space schedule, because a digest is a projection and capability-core schedules fire Model runs needing Control fire decisions. Add the reply-to-source error path for agent runs as a Model-side change tracked separately. Gate any ZDR-org digest on the content-free request class decision.
effortNote: Kept at L, but note the split: the digest alone is M once the ledger and a content-free class exist; finishing the ledger is roadmapped S4.4 work and larger than the digest.
verdictReason: Status is partial and already planned (S4.4); the item understates what exists (idempotency keys, lease worker, email channel config, a disabled brief scheduler), overstates what ZDR allows (the queue rejects ZDR), and places digest composition in the wrong plane.

exactGap: No call, huddle, SFU or WebRTC code exists in the frontend, gateway, Application, Model, Support or Endpoint planes (grep for livekit, mediasoup, RTCPeerConnection, webrtc, coturn, janus, jitsi matched only a Model Plane proto comment, and its generated Go, about an ephemeral realtime-session client secret for AI voice; the Support Plane runs a RustDesk relay for remote support, which is not an SFU). The Space header (SpacePage.tsx:358-377) has no call affordance, room liveness is a 6 s poll (SpacePage.tsx:87,298) with no push transport, and every room post is a Model turn sent through streamChat, so there is no human-only post path for a call card or companion chat. docs/space-defenition.md lists huddles among the non-goals (line 352), so this is both a code gap and an open product decision.
reuse: Control effect pattern for space.call.join: a deny-by-default *_entitled column on space_effect_policies plus a decision issuer in user-core/internal/spaces (migrations 018-028)
Convex spacePresence.ts heartbeat-with-TTL pattern and the lifecycle outbox/lease pattern for a spaceCalls projection fed by signed SFU webhooks
voice-recorder.ts mic error classification and the voice-mode-state.ts reducer discipline (the mic is never reopened silently)
Gateway /api/v1/ai/transcribe and /api/v1/ai/dictate (inference-core TranscribeSpeech) for post-call transcript, and the Meeting Scribe template in SpaceCreateAgentDialog.tsx for recap
Model Plane CreateRealtimeSession ephemeral-secret broker if an agent should join audio
activity-grammar.ts rows for call start and end; BrowserChrome.tsx live-frame WebSocket/EventSource as the only existing frontend push-transport precedent
constraints: Join must be minted by the gateway only after a Control decision for a new deny-by-default space.call.join effect (the policy table is per organisation) bound to the Control subject, never client-supplied identity. The call or meeting record belongs to the Application Plane keyed by spaceRef; do not add a child SpaceRef kind per call (registered kinds are personal, room, project, case, and each needs the Control registration saga). Revoking membership must end SFU access: tokens must be short-lived and the membership_changed event (best-effort plain NATS today) must close or kick the participant. ZDR: media is relayed and not stored; any transcript or recording is content and must follow ZDR, the Space deletion flow and the voice state machine's zdr-unavailable behaviour. An agent in a call must still be bound and invoked (no always-on presence). Three substrates are absent and owned by other items: push transport, human-only posts, and Space notifications. The documented non-goal must be reversed by a product decision.
approachAdjustment: Make the product-decision gate explicit and sequence calls after the human-only post path and a push or webhook-driven presence update, accepting a poll-based call card (6 s) for a first slice. Keep the Application-side record minimal (spaceCalls with state, started_by, server-derived attendees, policy and artifact refs) and defer the Buzz-style ephemeral child channel. Count the SFU/TURN deployment (Infra Plane) as a separate dependency.
effortNote: L covers only the call feature on a bought SFU; with the three absent substrates (push, human-only posts, ring notifications) counted it is XL.
verdictReason: Nothing exists today, the product doc lists huddles as a non-goal, and the feature rests on three absent substrates, so it should not sit in the top ranks; keep it as a later-wave, decision-gated item rather than drop it, since calls are table stakes in the Teams and Slack references.

exactGap: A durable, cross-device room-level read marker exists (Convex spaceReadMarkers, POST /spaces/{ref}/read, per-post 'New' badges derived against an arrival snapshot), but it was deliberately designed per room and not per thread (spaceReadMarkers.ts:4-12), the marker never moves backwards (advanceMarker), and there is no mark-unread, first-unread divider, jump-to-unread or receipts. Presence is room-scoped online/typing with a 30 s TTL and 8 s typing decay; the only global status is a manual profile availability value in user-core (online/busy/away/offline, no text or expiry) that no Space surface reads, and agent 'working' is only inferred in the browser from the polled thread projection. There are no Space saved items or reminders: only a personal Inbox follow-up and note calendar stored as user settings with no due-time trigger, and a 24 h snooze for support tickets.
reuse: Convex spaceReadMarkers table and the Application-owned own-row, content-free pattern; the SpacePage arrival snapshot and per-post 'New' flag for a first-unread divider and jump
Convex spacePresence heartbeat-with-TTL rows for status extension, and the user-core profile availability field as the home for status text and expiry
Convex ctx.scheduler.runAfter plus the outbox/lease pattern as the due-time trigger for refs-only reminders
notification-core feed (read, seen, archive) as the Inbox Reminders delivery surface
space-live-work.ts working-state derivation until a Model Plane run-state feed exists
capability-core Space-scoped cron schedules only for 'ask an agent to ping me if X is open' (an agent-authored scheduled run)
constraints: Read state and presence are Application-owned workspace projections and must stay content-free (timestamps against ids). The room marker was chosen over a per-thread frontier on purpose because the room renders every thread inline; a per-thread frontier only pays off once shared multi-turn threads exist (dependency F-t1-001), so do not build it first. Global status spans organisations, so it cannot live in a per-org Convex presence row without leaking; extend the Control profile value or keep org-scoped own-row writes. Agent availability needs an event or API feed from Model Plane (no cross-plane DB reads). Plain reminders should be Application-owned refs-only records fired by the Convex scheduler: capability-core schedules fire Model runs and every fire needs a Control schedule-fire decision, and an agent-created reminder for its owner is an owner action in the S2 sense (only tickets.create is supported today). Reminder target refs must be rechecked for access when the reminder fires. space-defenition.md lists presence polish among non-goals.
approachAdjustment: Split into three slices: (1) cheap wins on the existing marker: an explicit mark-unread mutation (advanceMarker never moves backwards by design), a first-unread divider and jump using the arrival snapshot already in SpacePage; (2) a status model that extends the existing user-core availability value with text and expiry, plus an agent working/waiting projection from a Model Plane feed; (3) personal saved items and reminders as refs-only Application records fired by the Convex scheduler, surfaced in the Inbox. Defer per-thread frontiers and receipts until shared threads exist, and drop the unverified 'priority re-notify' claim (notification-core has no priority, urgent or delayed-delivery concept).
effortNote: L as a bundle; slice 1 and the status extension are S-to-M, reminders are M, per-thread frontier and receipts are deferred.
verdictReason: Status is partial: the room marker, unread badges and room presence ship, and a deliberate per-room design decision conflicts with the per-thread frontier; the reminder trigger belongs in the Convex scheduler, not a Model Plane cron, and a profile status value already exists.

exactGap: The Spaces sidebar (CoreSidebarSpacesPanel.tsx:30-232) has fixed groups (Channels with the org room pinned first, Personal Space, All conversations of the selected room) plus a text filter, with no stars, custom sections, ordering, hide, mute or room-level unread badge, and the org WorkspaceSwitcher (CoreNavbar.tsx:672-729) has no cross-org badge or keyboard switching. A reusable organiser already exists for chat threads (ChatSidebarOrganizer.tsx and chat-organization.ts: custom projects, assignments, group/sort/filter views, native HTML5 drag with an accessible Move menu, a zod-typed action reducer) but it is browser-local (localStorage) and mounted for chat only. The item's 'unread is browser-local' premise is imprecise: the per-room marker is server-side in Convex, but sidebar unread dots come from a browser store populated only for rooms whose page was opened this session, and no cross-room or cross-org unread or attention aggregate exists.
reuse: ChatSidebarOrganizer native drag-and-drop with the accessible Move menu, and its zod-typed ChatOrganizationAction reducer, promoted to a server-synced preference document (this removes the 'no drag-and-drop library' concern)
listOrganizations and switchActiveOrganization behind the existing WorkspaceSwitcher for the cross-org list
activity-grammar.ts salience classes as the existing basis for a priority sort and computed system sections
Convex own-row, refs-only pattern (spaceReadMarkers, spacePresence) for the per-user preference document
server-pinned thread flag already relayed by the presentation route and the sidebar unread dot component
constraints: Each gateway request resolves exactly one authorised org (authorized_org_id from the active org), so cross-org badges need a deliberate multi-org read path that checks membership per target org and never mixes two orgs' data in one response (tenant and ZDR partition). Hide, mute and sort are presentation only and must never widen or narrow Space access; mute must be a notification preference distinct from agent pause. The preference document should store spaceRefs and ids, not room names, and live in the Application Plane as a per-user own-row record. Any server-computed attention summary must come from Application-owned read markers plus owner-plane events or APIs (approvals live in Model Plane), not DB reads. Solid 2.0 RC means prefer the existing native-drag pattern over a new library. The doc non-goals mention notification polish, which makes mute and system sections the least contentious part.
approachAdjustment: Correct the premise: unread is server-backed per room, so the missing dependency is a per-user, per-org attention summary (rooms with unread, waiting approvals), not 'server-side unread state'. First slice: stars, custom sections, hide, mute and per-group sort for Space rooms by promoting the chat organiser's pattern and action reducer to a synced Convex preference document; computed system sections (Unread, Waiting for approval, Agent runs, Muted) on top of the attention summary; cross-org badges and Ctrl+1..9 as a separate later item that needs the multi-org read path.
effortNote: M holds for the room-organisation slice reusing the existing organiser; the attention aggregate and cross-org badges are a separate L, so bundled it is L.
verdictReason: Status is partial for rooms and the pattern already exists for chat; the unread premise and the drag-and-drop concern are wrong, and cross-org badges need a different dependency than the item names.

exactGap: Only coarse removal exists: owners and managers can remove a member from a named room (remove_space_member to Convex spaceMemberGrants to Control roster sync), which Control publishes as aqencia.controlplane.space.membership_changed and session-core projects into space_membership_revocations to deny that subject's later run and thread access (I found no cancellation of in-flight runs). There is no report action, moderation queue, tombstone, per-user block list, timeout (suspended_until), ban (nothing stops re-adding) or removal of another member's post: thread presentation writes are owner-bound in Session Core, so even pinning someone else's post is refused. Agents carry no owner link in Control (space_memberships has subject_type 'service'; agents.createdBy in Application is optional provenance), so removing a person does not touch the agents they created.
reuse: remove_space_member and apply_room_membership (owner/manager gate, Convex grant list plus Control roster sync with honest 'unconfirmed' response)
Control membership_changed publisher and session-core space_membership_revocations consumer as the revocation hook to extend with a time-bounded sanction
spaceAgentBindings status paused/revoked and the PATCH/DELETE agent routes to pause a sanctioned person's agents in one room
Space activity feed rows and audit-core metadata for recording sanctions
Space deletion owner-receipt and outbox flow and the S6.1 thread erase as the basis for purge propagation
constraints: The content owner is Model Plane: room posts are Session Core threads and turns read through model-gateway under a Control thread-read decision, not Convex messages, so a tombstone that replaces content cannot live in convex-core; Application can hold only content-free reports and sanctions (refs and hash, no body under ZDR). Hiding or deleting another member's post needs a new Space-authorised write in Session Core (Control decision, mirroring model.thread.append), because presentation writes are owner-bound today. Suspension must be a Control membership fact (space_memberships has only active and revision, no suspended_until) so decision issuance refuses the subject; Application's spaceMemberGrants can only express 'editor' and there is no promote-to-manager path, so 'owners and managers' currently means the room creator. The agent cascade needs the agent-to-owner link recorded as a Control fact; the current revocation consumer is plain, non-JetStream NATS that explicitly tolerates missed events, too weak for a ban unless made durable or replayed. Removal must also propagate to Data Plane retrieval and graph indexes and notification payloads.
approachAdjustment: Move the tombstone and hide write to Session Core (Model Plane) behind a Space-authorised moderation decision, keep Application records content-free, and implement timeout and ban as Control membership state (suspended_until plus a sanction event on the existing membership_changed path made durable) instead of a separate moderation decision class unless proven necessary. Sequence behind room roles (F-t1-022) and the agent ownership link (F-t1-011), and note that today every post is an AI turn, so the first practical reports target agent output and prompts.
effortNote: Raised from L: it touches Control (schema, decision issuance), Model Plane (Session Core moderation write and purge), Application (reports, sanctions), Data Plane purge, a durable revocation event and the UI.
verdictReason: Status is partial (removal and revocation exist) while the moderation workflow is absent; the item puts tombstones in the wrong plane and understates the cross-plane cost, so reword the approach and raise effort.

exactGap: Named room creation takes a name only (create_personal_space routes kind=room to spaces:createRoomForGateway and refuses project and case with unsupported_space_kind at spaces.rs:2873), although the Convex schema and Control's registered_spaces already allow project and case kinds (no Convex mutation creates them). The only templates are three client-side agent prompt presets in SpaceCreateAgentDialog.tsx that prefill a name and instructions, with no agent roster, no seed artifacts and no clone, and the composer offers only actively bound agents and roster people as mention candidates (SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:184-203) with no offer to bind or invite. Nothing creates a case or project Space from a ticket: ticket.created appears only as an automation-rule event name in dispatchers.rs, and the ADR marks the support chat as a future case Space.
reuse: spaces:createRoomForGateway plus the Control registration saga (a created room registers within seconds per the page audit)
setInstructionsForGateway and GET/PATCH /instructions (4000-character Space instructions) as the template's instructions slot
Existing agent create and bind routes (POST /api/v1/spaces/{ref}/agents and /agents/bind) with binding policy fields (triggerModes, allowedTools, approvalMode) for the roster
add_space_member and sync_room_members for roster people, and require_space_agent_grant_role for the owner/manager gate
AGENT_TEMPLATES constants as the seed of a server-side template registry
constraints: A room is born pending_registration and nothing that depends on Control (membership convergence, agent binding decisions) can happen until Control registers it, so 'one transaction' is really an idempotent, resumable saga: create, await registration, set instructions, bind each agent through its own Control confirmation, then seed artifacts, reporting partial state honestly (the room doc says never say 'created' until both steps are confirmed). Templates must never pre-grant tools or approval modes beyond the binding defaults, and a mention never grants, so an invite or bind offer must go through add-member or bind decisions with the owner/manager role and must not reveal whether a private candidate exists. Project and case kinds are accepted by Control but their owner, lifecycle and membership semantics are not defined (ADR rows 82 and 84); a ticket-bound case Space needs a conversation-core event consumed by the Application Plane, with membership derived from assignees staying subordinate to the ticket ACL. Seed artifacts depend on the records item (F-t1-058). The Space doc non-goals do not exclude templates.
approachAdjustment: Reword 'one transaction' as a resumable saga and split the item: (1) templates as an org-level server-side registry of {instructions, agent roster with binding policy} executed over the existing create, instructions and bind routes, no seed artifacts; (2) offer to add a non-member person or bind an unbound agent from a mention, reusing add-member and bind decisions; (3) project and case kinds and ticket-bound case Spaces only after an ADR defines their owner and lifecycle; (4) seed canvas and list only after F-t1-058. Note the composer comment still points to a 'Phase UI-3b' bind offer that is not built, while the create-agent-from-room half of UI-3b shipped.
effortNote: Kept at L; slices (1) and (2) are about M, while case and project Spaces and seed artifacts are the L part.
verdictReason: Status is partial (name-only rooms, three client-side agent presets, project and case kinds accepted by Control but refused by the gateway); the approach needs a saga framing, a registry placement and a split, and the case-Space half depends on undefined ADR semantics.
